headline.headline: AVALANCHE BURY BLUES, 6-1, TO TAKE COMMANDING SERIES LEAD
headline.deck: Necas and Roy strike 23 seconds apart in a four-goal second period to blow open the game.
headline.body:
DENVER — Nicolas Roy and Martin Necas scored 23 seconds apart in a stunning second-period burst Saturday night, and the Colorado Avalanche dismantled the St. Louis Blues 6-1 to seize firm control of their second-round NHL playoff series. The four-goal second period turned what had been a competitive game into a rout, sending a sellout crowd at Ball Arena into full celebration before the third period even began.

The twin strikes from Roy and Necas within less than half a minute crushed whatever momentum the Blues had carried into the building. St. Louis, which had battled to stay within reach through the first period, simply had no answer for Colorado's speed and execution once the avalanche of goals began. The Blues managed just one goal in reply across the full sixty minutes.

The win puts Colorado in a position of strength heading into the next game of the series. The Blues now face the difficult task of regrouping after being thoroughly outclassed in one of the most lopsided results of this postseason. For the Avalanche, Roy and Necas have announced themselves as the defining playmakers of a deep and dangerous roster.

secondary.headline: WHITE SOX BLANK GUARDIANS, 3-0, BEHIND DOMINANT PITCHING STAFF
secondary.deck: Chicago's hurlers shut out Cleveland across nine innings, scoring all the damage in the fourth and seventh.
secondary.body:
CLEVELAND — The Chicago White Sox silenced Progressive Field on Saturday, shutting out the Cleveland Guardians 3-0 before 34,287 fans in a game completed in two hours and 49 minutes. Chicago's pitching staff allowed nothing across all nine innings, and the White Sox manufactured their offense in two bursts: a two-run fourth inning and a single run in the seventh.

The game was scoreless through the first three frames before Chicago broke through with a pair of runs in the fourth. The Guardians never threatened to answer, finishing the afternoon without a single run to show for their home date. The efficiency of Chicago's effort on the mound stood as the defining story of the afternoon at the lakefront ballpark.

secondary.headline: HEAT RUN RAPTORS OUT OF THE BUILDING IN TORONTO, 129-105
secondary.deck: Miami's overwhelming second-round victory signals a dangerous team firing on all cylinders.
secondary.body:
TORONTO — The Miami Heat arrived in Toronto for Game 2 of their second-round series and left no doubt about which team is the class of this matchup, rolling past the Raptors 129-105 in a performance that was not as close as the 24-point margin suggests. Miami's offense operated with efficiency throughout, pushing the lead past comfortable territory well before the final buzzer.

The Raptors, playing at home, could not contain Miami's attack and now find themselves in a deep hole in the series. The Heat have looked formidable throughout these playoffs, and Saturday's result in Scotiabank Arena will only deepen concern in Toronto about what adjustments, if any, can slow this Miami squad down before the series gets further out of hand.

secondary.headline: RAYS EDGE YANKEES, 1-0, AS ARANDA HOMER PROVES THE DIFFERENCE
secondary.deck: Jonathan Aranda's solo shot in the third inning is all Tampa Bay needs to shut out New York.
secondary.body:
ST. PETERSBURG — Jonathan Aranda hit a solo home run in the third inning Saturday night, and the Tampa Bay Rays made it stand up for a 1-0 shutout of the New York Yankees before 40,542 at Tropicana Field. The game was played in two hours and 30 minutes, with Tampa Bay's pitching staff protecting that single run from the third inning all the way through a scoreless ninth.

New York had no answer for the Rays' arms across eight innings after the Yankees went down in order for long stretches. The Yankees did not generate enough sustained pressure to threaten the lead, and a pinch-hit strikeout for McMahon in the ninth closed the door on New York's final hopes. The loss was a frustrating end to the afternoon for a Yankee lineup that generated little offense throughout.

column.headline: COLORADO'S ONE-TWO PUNCH MAKES AVALANCHE THE TEAM TO BEAT OUT WEST
column.body:
Twenty-three seconds. That is all the time that separated Nicolas Roy's goal from Martin Necas's in the second period Saturday night, and those 23 seconds may well have settled the fate of the St. Louis Blues for this postseason. When a team can score twice before an opponent can even retrieve the puck from the net, it is not a hot streak. It is a statement. The Colorado Avalanche are playing the kind of hockey that wins championships, and the rest of the Western Conference bracket ought to be paying close attention.

The Blues are not a bad team. They earned their way into the second round and came to Denver with credible professional players. But credible is not enough when Colorado's skill players are moving at full speed and the puck seems to find the net almost at will. The Avalanche have the depth, the goaltending, and the firepower to make a serious run at the Stanley Cup. Roy and Necas announced that on Saturday night, and this city of hockey fans will be riding that wave for days.

story.headline: BREWERS SURVIVE PADRES IN NLDS GAME 1 THRILLER, 3-2
story.deck: Milwaukee's roof becomes unlikely hero as Brewers draw first blood in playoff series
story.body:
MILWAUKEE — The roof at American Family Field played defense Saturday night, helping the Milwaukee Brewers escape with a 3-2 victory over the San Diego Padres in Game 1 of the National League Division Series before 42,843 fans. The Brewers, who finished the regular season 103-59 and atop the NL, now hold a 1-0 series lead heading into Sunday's Game 2.

The Brewers trailed 2-0 after the Padres pushed across two runs in the second inning, but Milwaukee answered with a pair of their own in the third. Jesse Chourio and William Contreras each connected for home runs to power the Brewers offense, while Turang and Mitchell contributed stolen bases to keep San Diego's pitching off balance. Milwaukee took the lead for good with a run in the seventh, the decisive blow coming after a pinch-hit single. Wild pitches from both sides complicated matters — Misiorowski and Ashby were each charged with hit batters, plunking Trey France and Jake Bauers respectively.

The Padres, who left a stunning 22 runners on base, had a potential late rally snuffed out in part by the stadium's retractable roof in the ninth inning, turning what San Diego believed was a fair-ball opportunity into an out that preserved the one-run margin. The Padres, 91-71 during the regular season and NL West runners-up, will send their Game 2 starter to the mound Sunday afternoon looking to even the series before it shifts to San Diego.

story.headline: HEAT TORCH RAPTORS IN SEASON OPENER, ROLL TO 24-POINT ROAD WIN IN TORONTO
story.deck: Miami dominates from wire to wire, handing Toronto a lopsided opening-night defeat.
story.body:
TORONTO -- The Miami Heat wasted no time announcing themselves on the road, dismantling the Toronto Raptors 129-105 Saturday night at Scotiabank Arena in what amounted to a dominant, wire-to-wire performance to open the 2026-27 NBA season. Miami controlled the tempo from the opening tip and never allowed Toronto to establish any rhythm, sending a clear message to the rest of the Eastern Conference.

The Heat built their advantage methodically through each quarter, pushing the margin into double digits early and never surrendering the cushion. Toronto, playing in front of its home crowd on opening night, could not find answers defensively or generate enough consistent offense to threaten Miami's grip on the game. The final 24-point margin reflected just how thoroughly the Heat controlled proceedings in Canada.

Off the court, the NBA world was buzzing Sunday with news that Los Angeles Lakers forward Ziaire Williams proposed to his longtime girlfriend during Bruno Mars's second Inglewood concert stop, while LeBron James drew massive crowds at a Philadelphia 76ers scrimmage, calling the session a great first step for his new squad alongside Jaylen Brown. The regular season tips off in under a month.

story.headline: SCHMALTZ SPARKS MAMMOTH TO HOT 2-0 START AS UTAH HEADS TO NEW YORK
story.deck: Nick Schmaltz's two-goal performance lifts Utah atop the Central Division standings.
story.body:
Nick Schmaltz delivered a two-goal performance to push the Utah Mammoth to an unblemished 2-0 record in the Central Division, setting the stage for a marquee road test Sunday when Utah visits the New York Rangers at Madison Square Garden. The Mammoth enter the matchup as one of the early-season surprises in the Western Conference, while New York brings a 2-1 record in the Metropolitan Division and the home-ice advantage of one of hockey's most storied arenas.

Elsewhere around the league Saturday, the San Jose Sharks improved to 2-0 in the Pacific Division by grinding out an overtime victory, giving them a full head of steam heading into a Sunday clash with the Dallas Stars, who sit at 0-2 in the Central Division and are already searching for answers early in the young season. The Sharks' ability to close out games in extra time signals a resilience that could make them a factor in a crowded Pacific race.

In Atlantic Division action, the Ottawa Senators arrive in Boston at 1-0 to face a Bruins squad sitting at 2-1, while the Philadelphia Flyers carry a three-game losing streak into Tampa Bay to face a Lightning team at 1-1. Out west, the Calgary Flames, winless at 0-2, visit the Seattle Kraken on Sunday in a Pacific Division matchup both clubs need badly.

story.headline: QUARTERBACK CAROUSEL SPINS WILDLY AS NFL OFFSEASON HEATS UP
story.deck: Three veteran signal-callers change addresses as rosters reshape ahead of training camp
story.body:
The NFL's offseason reshuffling reached a fever pitch this week as front offices across the league scrambled to lock up talent before minicamp rosters solidify. The Cleveland Browns made the boldest move, acquiring veteran quarterback Sam Darnold from the Minnesota Vikings in exchange for a second-round pick and a depth linebacker, giving offensive coordinator Tommy Rees a proven starter to build around after yet another lost season on Lake Erie. The deal reunites Darnold with receivers coach Chad Morton, who tutored him during his brief resurgence in Carolina two seasons ago.

The free-agent market continued churning as well. Wide receiver Curtis Samuel agreed to a two-year, $18 million deal with the Pittsburgh Steelers, giving new head coach Mike Vrabel a shifty slot weapon to complement his rebuilt offense. The Las Vegas Raiders, meanwhile, inked defensive tackle Derrick Brown to a three-year contract worth $54 million, a signal that the franchise intends to anchor its defense up front after finishing 28th in run defense during the 2025 campaign.

NFL draft analysts have spent the spring dissecting how teams used their picks from April's draft in Newark, with the Jacksonville Jaguars drawing particular praise for selecting Tennessee defensive end James Pearce Jr. and pairing him immediately with edge rusher Josh Hines-Allen. General manager James Gladstone called the combination a cornerstone for the next half-decade. Training camps across the league open in late July, and competition for starting jobs is expected to be fierce from Foxborough to Santa Clara.
